We looked over to see if the community had suitable candidates, and sometimes it either takes time for them to improve or if they aren't up to the job at all. replies.author: Fouled
replies.body:
Alright. Let me shine some light on all of this. 

First of all. We decided to pick senior moderators to take on the role of map developer because they were trustworthy (as Para said). We would teach them in map making, YML and Github, then they would be able to help us. Most of the recently promoted Admin(s)/Senior moderators got off to an excellent start and have already learnt Github and some parts of YML. They are really active, maintaining the job of both senior moderator/admin and map developer. Most of the senior/admin moderators we choose have some recognition with maps. 

Second of all. We don't think anyone in the community is currently ready for map developer. Yes, of course we have our reasons for this, and they are quite solid. I'm not going to share them on the forums or with anyone individually.

If you have anymore questions or complaints regarding this topic, feel free to message me on Skype - Slicornplaysminecraft.

replies.author: Ogrey
replies.body:
Why does the staff and mapdevs try so hard?
Just gonna point something out, Map Developer are also Staff Members, and are, in fact, just above Moderators in https://avicus.net/staff

So why the hell not give the community what it wants?
You wanted CTW? CTW you have.
You wanted SG? SG you have.
You wanted regulars to become Map Developers? You have Para, me, Sky, Sli, Polar, and Pavlo. Merlin was ultimately promoted while he was a Moderator, too, but of course he deserved it.
Thing is, there are no more candidates that we personally consider to be fit for the rank. You guys think it's all about building maps and making half-assed YMLs, and it's not like that. As a Map Developer you must be trustworthy, you must be active, you must make maps on a regular basis, be able to make fully-working YMLs, as well as spotting errors on them fastly and being able to fix them. You must possess the ability to identify what kind of content is up to standards to be on Avicus (speaking map-wise), you must have an organized work ethic, you must have good roots with the community, you must prove to be able to work as a team, you must meet a lot of standards, so it's not that simple to just pick new Map Developers.

replies.author: Ogrey
replies.body:
Now, my thoughts regarding this.
Just a day after I retired from my positions as a Staff Member, I was incredibly shocked to see Senior Staff members taking over the role as Map Developers.
There were clearly some questions spinning around my head, and I was wondering what made the team take that decision.
So well, as I was given back my rank as a Map Developer, I became aware of the reasons as to why this happened.

Apparently we weren't enough just yet and we needed to get some work off our shoulders. Alright, my honest opinion to this is we don't really have that much hard work to do. The update already happened (and we didn't even get to finish the YMLs for all CTW maps, and yeah, we had months to do so) and there's barely any heavy work left to do. The Map Reassessment was probably our most top priority work, and to be honest it wasn't even hard. I rejoined the team and I successfully gave valid feedback for every single one map in the doc in a matter of hours, while some of my mates had a week to do so and they didn't finish it.
Exactly what kind of work are we supposed to take off our shoulders? I recall CTW and SG being the most important things to do and I pretty much contributed a lot to what concerns SG in terms of maps (gathered the majority) and YML (also YMLed some).
About CTW, we have a big amount of maps in the repository that haven't been YMLed yet, and if this is the work that we're supposed to avoid, hence why we promoted new people, then you guys really have left me shocked. Pretty sure our work is easy, why? because we all meet the standards and requirements to have our position, that's why it's easy and that's why we are all able to do it.
We aren't other networks that get a bunch of maps submitted to them, we're still growing, and there's not that many maps, we could easily handle all of it if we all worked hard enough, but I'm gonna be honest and say we've all been rather lazy lately, including myself. We aren't very organized, there are things we must all improve on and avoiding our work or taking it off our shoulders isn't a solution.

Now, regarding the recent promotions, okay. They were promoted already. What can we do? demote them? I don't think that's a solution. They were already promoted, what can we do? I was really happy to see Mango hyped for his training, Michael was also very excited to help, I saw Peachy being pretty enthusiast about it and Pel still needs to be trained, but I know he'll do great.
I trained Mango on his GitHub lessons, and he took the hang of it quite quickly, it wasn't a trouble, and I am pretty sure he'll do a great work. That's true, anyone can be a Map Developer, they just need to be teached everything once they are promoted, they can even be teached how to build if necessary, and how to code YML. Thing is, trust is a very important factor. Do we want a regular to just go rogue someday and leak the whole repository and ruin Avicus? Senior Staff members have already proved to be trustworthy. That's a very important reason as to why they were promoted, and I'm glad they were chosen out of everyone (even though I don't fully agree).

Alright, now, let me ask a question, after what I said in previous paragraphs stating our somewhat lazy and poor work ethic, do we really need more Map Developers? or do we just need to improve? I believe we should be much more organized in the way we do stuff. Let's not go candidate-hunting, but if we notice there's some outstanding member out there that we can keep an eye out for, then why not? We should only promote players (Staff included, because why not? Jozz and Mango are great builders imo, I love Crescent series and Dredmor <3) whenever we feel they're ready and that they meet the standards. If they meet the standards, the rank will be easy to handle, because if they don't, then it'll be hard. It's just like an exam, if you study and know the answers, it'll be easy, and if we don't study, it'll be hard.

Last thing I have to say about this is that we should not just go promoting people lately because we need to take work off our shoulders, as I said, there's no heavy work to do, there's just the usual accept-deny maps and if someone's gonna bring up the tourney to counter anything I say, I believe we're enough already, but we need to work way more efficiently.
Thanks for reading all of this, if you did, it really shows you're actually interested in the subject.

Thanks for reading all of this, if you did, it really shows you're actually interested in the subject.

replies.author: Robin_DD_J
replies.body:
Alright so I might aswell chare my thoughts. I won't deny it, it would be cool to have mapdev, but after all I always care about the people around me. People are what makes things possible, without players, we wouldn't have the server. It's imporatant to see what they are able to do. The communinty is what makes the game. Let's take Kohi for an example, every time I join that server I see atleast 20 people screaming eZ, I was "lagging", you're such a pinger. Whatever I say, but the point is that these rude people, make others rude, that's why I was rude when I first came to avicus. Avicus is a very nice community imo, but I won't deny it, some people can annoy me a lot. 
 Staff usually get their rank, because others see them as something special. But when a player gets mod or higher, they get a job, they will work for the server, no matter what rank they are, they are doing something for the server. The higher rank you have, the more special you are. This also gives you responsibilities, like handpicked staff. Well my point with that rant right there is that, sr.mods or higher got "a lot" of stuff to do atm. And you said something about truthworthy?  Well yeah, they are! But how do you know that regs are not truthworthy? If you talk with someone on, let's say ts you usually can see their personality after just 15 mins. And think about it, giving a reg mapdev means he will be able to focus more on his own job, istead of having to make a map, hand picking staff, making a tournament possible and still have to be nice to players. And you should be able to do that without any problems. But, I'm not against sr.mods or higher getting staff, I'm against it if they can't handle it. 
 But something that also made me a bit, annoyed was the fact that you were going to learn them? Are you serious? Instead of doing that, help players on the YML thread now when the docs.avicus is down. I asked something like 3 days ago now, still havn't got an answer. If they actually don't know how to make a fully creative map and a YML, they don't deserve mapdev. And you should actually, contact us regs who think got a chance, and ask them if they would like a lesson or two.
 The last thing I got to say is. This community complain, because they actually see reasons. Yes, some people do it because that's how they are. But every time I complain, I have a reason. Staff who can't judge if it's aimbot or kill aura? Do I care about the staff? No. Do I care about the players being effected by it? Yes. You really shouldn't teach a player who got the rank, to know the difference, they get a rank because they know what they are doing, otherwise they need to learn it by themself or actually ask someone that knows private.

Please don't take offence, but once Evo have to make a 700 word paragraph why they are right or wrong, something isn't right.

/Robin

replies.author: StewieFG
Zintenka
replies.body:
I bothered with reading your whole thing and you raise a lot of very great points.

I've looked from both perspectives and im trying to understand both so as to not be a narcissistic asshole.

Well, from the mapdev's POV, they handpicked the senior moderators because they were very well trusted and some of them had prior knowledge of YMLs and mapmaking (Take Merlin for example. He is a beast with maps).
And in regards to the map-reassessment they were just removing some maps to make some edits, I even gave in some in put on what to do to Teres to make it more fun and last longer. 

Now, onto the player's POV, you guys raise a lot of good points. Like what about the senior mods who do not make maps on a regular basis? What about the ones who do not know how to YML? Why give them YML lessons, isnt that biased if you do not teach the whole community? Why not give mapdev to ones who actually deserve it? *Cough* Me *Cough* *Cough*

ANYWAY ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Well Uncle Zintenka the Observer and Analyzer and Mediator will try his hardest to answer your questions based on observations and reasoning.

Like what about the senior mods who do not make maps on a regular basis? I do not know why they were promoted, but I guess it had something to do with the fact that they were very well trusted.

What about the ones who do not know how to YML? Again, I do not know about this one but its the same guess as the first.

Why give them YML lessons, isnt that biased if you do not teach the whole community? This one, I have absolutely no way to answer, you guys got me stumped on this one. And I'm wondering this one myself as well...

Why not give mapdev to ones who actually deserve it? AAAAAAAaaaaaaahhhhhh...~ The powder keg of all questions! The one that is the most sensitive! Ye, this one gets me a bit peeved myself mapdevs in all honesty. There are certain players in the community who are long-time dedicators of mapmaking for Avicus who have not gotten the rank yet. I will not give out names as y'all know who you are.

My analyses: The mapdevs are stressed and overworked. They work too hard and after the update, with CTW and SG being re-added their brains got a shot of Dopamine, the glory hormone that makes one feel very good. 

But with all the events of: "Avicus is copy OCN!" "Sr.Mods are mapdevs!?" Their Dopamine of their bodies are receding and they are becoming very stressed out. 

Now, I'm not saying to stop making topics like these, because these topics are needed to sort out problems and concerns.

But what I am saying is to give constructive criticism, give great points and do not post the topic in a "WHAT THE FUCK ARE YOU DOING!?" manner and in a "Hey mapdevs, there were some senior moderators that were recently promoted, we would like to know why is that and what is happening?" manner.
